_readme: THE LIVE TO-DO LIST, AS DATA. This file is the source. to-do.md's ranked table is
GENERATED from it by `npm run to-do`, and the Handbook's ranking control reads it.
Edit here — an edit to that table is overwritten.
A list saved from the control comes back with `npm run to-do -- <file>`. It is
validated against the five fields first, and an item Mike settles is NOT removed
until its closure is written on to-do-done-and-parked.md — the command applies
nothing at all until then. An item gone from both pages is an item nobody knows
existed.
FORMATTING IS THE SCRIPT'S. Applying a saved list rewrites this file with two-space
JSON, so do not hand-tune the layout; it will not survive.
Every item must carry all five fields the list's own rules demand — score, why,
risk, askedBy, touches — and tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js fails the build if one
is missing. That guard is the whole reason this file exists: an item missing a
field is a note, and notes are what produced two pieces of unrequested work on
ORDER IS MIKE'S RANKING. The array order is the order on screen. It is not
computed from the score, and it must never be re-sorted by a script or a session.
Where his order and the score disagree, his order wins and the score stays
visible so the disagreement is on the page.
SCORE — 5 security/privacy/data integrity · 4 the user is worse off · 3 helps
sell the package · 2 robustness · 1 internal only · 0 is not filed, it is
deleted with its code.
askedBy.ours = true means NOBODY OUTSIDE ASKED. It is not a defect to record it;
it is a defect to hide it. An item that cannot name Mike or a named outsider has
to justify itself.
orderSource: the Handbook ranking control (scripts/handbook-shell.html), saved by Mike on 2026-08-15. It replaced design/mockups/to-do-list-table.html, which set the order before it.

items.name: The 21 branches that still name a page nobody can open
items.why: Of the 55 recommendations across the logic tables, 28 lose text to the template gate because they name a page that does not exist in the 291-record library. Seven were the Get Seminar branches, fixed 2026-08-15 once Mike named the real page (Design & Deliver). The other 21 sit in the fmc_, cas_, fbp_ and ol_ tables and nobody has looked at them.
items.risk: 21 branches of Mike's own coaching are cut back or withheld before they reach an adviser. The gate is behaving correctly; the content names tools that are not there. Each one is advice an adviser is not getting, and nothing on screen says so.

askedBy.detail: 2026-08-15 — "put them in the list of to dos", after being shown that the seven Seminar branches were seven of twenty-eight. Found by us; filed on his instruction.

items.touches: data/logic_trees.json, the Mentor Hub logic tables, and the Template Check screen where the real page names are settled.
items.note: RANKED LAST DELIBERATELY, and it scores 4. Mike's ruling the same day: clear the technical and feature work first so the master team can start UAT testing, THEN double back to wording and document-title alignment. This is wording and title alignment. The pattern is proven and cheap once a name is known — the Seminar seven took five words and a seven-line diff — but each of the 21 needs the REAL page name, and that is Mike's to give, never a developer's to rule on. Put the actual sentences in front of him, not the label: that is what unblocked 2.3 after four sessions.

items.name: A screen can show one row when 67 exist, and say nothing
items.why: The mentor's Advisory Distinctions tab showed 1 distinction when the shipped set is 67. A local, git-ignored dev file (data/dev-platform-distinctions.json) is deliberately preferred over the committed seed when there is no database, and one stale test row in it shadowed all 67 — with nothing on screen saying so.
items.risk: Anyone developing, demoing or reviewing reads what is on screen as the real platform set. It cost most of a session to diagnose, and the same pattern applies to every dev-JSON fallback in the app, not just this one.

askedBy.detail: He spotted it himself on the Mentor Hub, 2026-08-16 — 'the advisory distinctions ... no longer appear to be linked and working at mentor level'. Diagnosed the same session.

items.touches: server/utils/platformDistinctions.js and every other dev-JSON fallback (firmDistinctions, quizzes, coaching, currency); the Mentor Hub Advisory Distinctions tab.
items.note: THE LOCAL SYMPTOM IS FIXED BY DELETING THE FILE — Mike was given the command on 2026-08-16 because the AI's own safety guard refused the deletion. THE ITEM IS THE UNDERLYING FAULT, not that file: a screen served from a dev fallback must SAY it is, e.g. 'showing local dev data — 67 shipped rows are being shadowed'. Same family as 4.16 and the same lesson: the content was there, the screen was there, and nothing connected the two or admitted the gap. Verify the fix by loading the tab with and without the local file, not by reading the loader.

items.name: The AI invents advice when it is routed to the wrong method
items.why: A Dashboard Discussions question was routed by the engine to the Ratio Analysis coaching tree. The AI then produced its own plausible 'tactical options' and 'discussion questions' for the metric rather than saying it had none for it. Two faults stacked: the wrong guide was selected, and the model filled the gap instead of admitting it.
items.risk: An adviser reads invented content as Mike's authored method and takes it to a client. It is indistinguishable from the real thing on screen — it has the right headings, the right tone and the right shape. This is the precise failure 4.16 spent five sessions closing from the other direction: 4.16 was authored content that never arrived; this is unauthored content that arrives looking authored, and it is the worse of the two because nothing about it looks wrong.

askedBy.detail: Found by us on 2026-08-17 while verifying item 4.16 F on the running app — the first Dashboard Discussions attempt came back with invented questions. Reported to Mike the same session and HE RULED IT ONTO THE LIST: 'if you found this problem then yes - it gets put on the to do list'. Written into RELEASE-NOTES-v0.9.0.md §4a so the master team is not surprised by it in UAT.

items.touches: server/utils/logicTrees.js (detectLogicTree, detectLogicTrees) and pickLearnTreeAI in server/advisorEngine.js for the routing half; the learn-mode prompt for the honesty half.
items.note: TWO HALVES, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE ITEM. Sharpening the routing reduces how often it happens and can never remove it — some questions are genuinely ambiguous, and Ratio Analysis and Dashboard Discussions are neighbouring methods. THE FAULT WORTH FIXING IS THAT THE MODEL DOES NOT SAY 'I DO NOT HAVE THAT FOR THIS METHOD.' Do not close this item on a routing tweak alone. VERIFY THE WAY 4.16 WAS VERIFIED — ask a real question on the running app and compare the answer word for word against the source file, because every automated test here passes on an answer the model made up.

items.name: Nothing in this project ever checks that a screen LOOKS right
items.why: CLAUDE.md's testing standard names Playwright for critical journeys. It is not in package.json and never has been. Jest runs under jsdom, which has NO layout engine: it cannot measure a width, a gap or an overflow, so a screen whose boxes are squashed, whose columns collapse or whose table runs off the page passes all 5,887 tests. Every visual defect this project has had was found by a human opening the page, and only after it shipped.
items.risk: It has already happened twice and both times the finder was Mike. On 2026-08-18 the Property Tax Rules tab shipped with five phasing percentage boxes sharing a slot sized for one — about 31px each — so every one read as empty while holding and saving the correct value; he found it by opening the tab. On 2026-08-21 the five-property screen shipped with layout stated as UNVERIFIED in its own design document because there was no way to check it. Until something can see a rendered page, "the tests are green" will keep meaning less than it sounds, and the product owner will keep being the visual regression suite.

askedBy.detail: Raised 2026-08-21 while closing 4.19, when the screen could not be visually verified before shipping and that had to be written into the design document as a gap. It stays because it is the named standard in CLAUDE.md going unmet, not a new idea — and because the two defects it would have caught were both found by Mike rather than by us. Adding a browser driver is a dependency change and needs his explicit approval under the Stack Constitution.

items.touches: package.json (a dev dependency and a script), a new tests/visual/ directory, and the CI step. Playwright is the version named in CLAUDE.md; whatever is chosen must install and run on the locked Node 14.15 target or the choice is not compliant — check that BEFORE proposing a version.
items.note: DO NOT INSTALL ANYTHING WITHOUT MIKE SAYING YES — this is a dependency change and the Stack Constitution is one-directional: if a driver does not fit Node 14.15, the answer is a different driver, never a raised floor. Scope it to a handful of screenshots of the report screens at one width, not a full visual-regression suite; the goal is to SEE the page, not to pin every pixel.

items.name: The property drawing promises a per-property tax override that nothing builds
items.why: The Tax rules card on design/mockups/multiple-property-portfolio.html carries the note "A single property may still differ — that override lives on the property itself, below." No such control is drawn anywhere on that page, and none is built: the tax rules are portfolio-level and apply to all five properties. The drawing's prose promises a control the drawing itself never shows.
items.risk: This is the artefact and the build disagreeing, which is the precise thing §10 exists to catch. Building it unasked would ship something Mike never saw; deleting the sentence would hide the promise. Left alone and unrecorded it becomes a claim a later session believes because it is written down — the failure mode design-docs-are-claims-to-check describes, in an approved artefact rather than a plan.

askedBy.detail: Raised 2026-08-21 while naming the twelve build-vs-drawing differences in §10. It stays because the honest options are opposite — build the control, or strike the sentence — and only Mike can say which. It blocks nothing either way.

items.touches: Either components/MultiplePropertyAssessment.vue and locales/en.json (build the override), or one sentence in design/mockups/multiple-property-portfolio.html plus the §10 row (strike it). Whichever way it goes, §10 of design/MULTIPLE-PROPERTY-ASSESSMENT.md records the outcome.
items.note: ASK, DO NOT CHOOSE. A firm advising across a border is the case for a per-property override; a family having one country is the case against, and that is the reasoning the card is built on today (§11 Q11).

items.name: An accountant can share a prompt and have it checked — designed, drawn, not built
items.why: Mike asked for a place a firm manager can put a prompt they believe in, have it checked against our protocols, and get back what is good, what is missing and what conflicts — accepting or declining each suggestion. The design and the screen are committed (design/PROMPT-CONTRIBUTION-SAFETY.md, design/mockups/prompt-contribution.html, `4a7c47e`) and four of his rulings are already folded into them. NOTHING IS BUILT.
items.risk: It is the first path in this app by which user-authored free text reaches a model, so it is the one feature where getting the ORDER wrong matters: the refusal screen is step 2 of the build for a reason. A refusal path built last is a refusal path built badly — and it is the screen an innocent accountant meets when their working document contains a real client name, which is the check most likely to fire and least likely to be anybody doing anything wrong.

askedBy.detail: 2026-08-22 — "they also need a place they can 'drag and drop' their AI prompts - click 'Analyse against existing protocols' and get a summary report of the pros and cons, what should be included with the ability to accept or decline the changes", then narrowed by him to pasted text only: "if pasting the wording (they copy and paste from their own source doc) is better security then that's what we require - and we explain this to them for their own clients protection."

items.touches: A new Restify route calling server/utils/openaiClient.js through server/utils/promptSafety.fenceUntrusted + stripInvisible; deterministic refusal checks with their own tests; a new panel on the AI Prompts page; and four AI-response validation tests (valid, malformed, missing fields, wrong types) per CLAUDE.md.
items.note: 🔴 BUILD ORDER IS §7 OF THE DESIGN AND IT IS NOT ARBITRARY. 1) the paste box, with the explanation of WHY we do not take files sitting beside it rather than behind a help link. 2) the deterministic refusals AND the blocked screen together. 3) the AI review. 4) — separately, later, and NOT in the same breath — storing a contribution as reference material the AI draws on. Steps 1–3 change nothing about how advice is produced; step 4 is the one that moves the app’s risk profile. ⚠ RULED, DO NOT RE-OPEN: pasted text only, no file uploads EVER (uploads are ruled OUT, not deferred — reinstating them is a new decision); nobody above signs a contribution off, because a level’s material is its own and is OFFERED downward under P11; and the AI review is an advisor, never a gatekeeper — "the AI said it was fine" must never be what admits text into a prompt. ⚠ AND DO NOT let this item pull the Advisory Staircase, Distinctions, Quizzes or Domain Support into scope: see the boundary paragraph under P11 in features/tier-cascade.md, which exists because an earlier draft of P11 nearly did exactly that.

items.name: A template's tutorial video gets attached to a calculator that shares its name
items.why: server/utils/videoInjector.js appends 'A 24-minute tutorial video is available in Advisor-e to help you prepare' after ANY bolded name that matches a template holding a video. Since 2026-08-22 the AI may also name a CALCULATION MODEL in its answer, and two model names are also template names: Working Capital Cycle and Quick Position. Seen live: the calculator line read 'Working Capital Cycle — ... open it at /business-performance-report' followed immediately by the 24-minute video sentence. The video is real, and it belongs to the TEMPLATE of that name, not to the calculator page the advisor was just pointed at.
items.risk: Small and specific: an advisor goes looking for a tutorial about a calculator screen and finds a video about a different thing with the same name. It is not a fabrication — the video exists — which is what makes it easy to miss. It cannot be fixed in the prompt: the injector runs AFTER the AI has written the answer and matches on bold text alone, so telling the AI to write differently only moves the problem.

askedBy.detail: Found 2026-08-22 while testing item 4.32 against the running app. Raised rather than fixed in passing, because videoInjector is a shipped, tested utility and the honest options differ in cost — see the note.

items.touches: server/utils/videoInjector.js and its test, or data/report-model-summaries.json if the answer is to rename. Nothing in the prompts.
items.note: 🔴 THE PROMPT CANNOT FIX THIS, and an earlier attempt made things worse — instructing the AI not to bold a model name stripped the bold off the TEMPLATE name too, which is the very thing the injector reads. Reverted. ⚠ TWO HONEST OPTIONS, and they are not equivalent: (1) teach the injector to skip a line that carries a calculator page path, which is narrow and cheap but is pattern-matching on output shape; (2) accept it — the video is real and same-named material is arguably relevant, so nothing is untrue, just imprecise. There is a third that is NOT ours: renaming a model or a template is Mike's call and would ripple through the catalogue, the summaries and the template library. ⚠ AFFECTS EXACTLY TWO NAMES TODAY. Adding a model whose name matches a template widens it, which is worth knowing before the next one is catalogued.

items.name: The Model Guide search only matches the exact words the page happens to use
items.why: The search on /model-guide matches ONE whole phrase against one joined string: haystack(m).includes(q) in components/ModelGuide.vue. So it finds a model only when the advisor happens to type a run of words that appears verbatim in that model's own text. It cannot match two words that are both present but not adjacent, and it knows no synonyms - the property model calls its subject 'property' and 'rental', so an advisor who thinks in 'houses' is told the library holds nothing.
items.risk: REPRODUCED IN THE RUNNING APP, 2026-08-23, exactly as Mike reported: 'Investing in houses' returns 'no models match' while the Multiple Property Assessment model sits in the library. It is not one unlucky phrase - 'houses' returns nothing, and so does 'investment property', because those two words never sit next to each other in the text. Only the single word 'property' or 'rental' finds it. The screen exists so an advisor can choose the right model BEFORE opening one; a search that answers 'nothing here' to a fair description of what they want defeats the page, and does it silently - the advisor concludes the product cannot help rather than that the search is narrow.

askedBy.detail: Reported by Mike on 2026-08-23 while looking at the Model Guide: 'the search function in the models summary is too literal. I typed "Investing in houses" and it failed to find the property assessment model.' Verified the same day by driving the running page rather than by reading the code.

items.touches: What else moves if this moves? Only the Model Guide search. The catalogue, the models and the report screens are untouched - this is how the page filters what it already has.
items.note: TWO SEPARATE FAULTS, and the cheap one is not the interesting one. (1) WHOLE-PHRASE MATCHING: split the query into words and require every word to appear somewhere in the haystack, which fixes 'investment property' and any other pair of words the advisor uses in their own order. (2) NO VOCABULARY: 'houses', 'landlord', 'rental yield' are what an advisor says; 'property' is what the page says. That needs a small authored synonym list per model - and under CLAUDE.md's hub-page rule, authored content the product reads belongs on a screen, not buried in a component. CHECK FIRST whether data/report-model-summaries.json is the right home for it, beside the model's other authored lines, rather than inventing a second store. DO NOT reach for fuzzy matching or an embedding search: this library holds ~18 models, and a wrong-but-confident match is worse here than a miss, because the advisor takes the suggestion into a client meeting.

items.name: The five drivers are defined in two places, and the copies can drift
items.why: Learning Psychology carries the source definitions of the five drivers of human output, transcribed from the master app's own Productive Habits template. data/staff-domain-support.json paraphrases the same five in its "5 Drivers of Human Output - Performance Diagnosis" row, where they serve a diagnosis rather than a definition. Both reach the advisor. Found 2026-08-23, recorded but not reconciled. Mike's call: which one is the source, and should the other quote it.
items.risk: Two copies of the same authored content is how content drifts apart in this repo - the 4.16 sweep exists because of exactly that. Corrected in one place and not the other, the AI is given two different definitions of the same five drivers.

askedBy.detail: Found during the Learning Psychology build, 2026-08-23. Nobody outside asked.

items.note: Written into the 2026-08-23 session notes and it reached no list until 2026-08-24 - one of the two items that prompted the session-notes rule change.

items.name: Whether Learning Psychology should reach the AI on every recommendation
items.why: The page reaches the AI only alongside Facilitation 101's learn reference. At around 6,000 characters, putting it on every client recommendation is a real cost per call and was deliberately not made the default when it shipped on 2026-08-23. Mike's call: leave it as it is, put it on every recommendation, or gate it on something.
items.risk: Left unasked it stays at the accidental setting rather than a chosen one - and the advice the AI gives is shaped by whether it can see the psychology or not.

askedBy.detail: Raised as an open question when Learning Psychology shipped, 2026-08-23.

items.note: Appended at the end of the array because the order is Mike's ranking and no session re-sorts it. He ranks these two when he is ready.

items.name: Sweep the frozen ACTIONS.md for anything that is genuinely still open
items.why: ACTIONS.md was frozen on 2026-08-24 at 7,400+ lines because it had become unreadable - /startup already steered sessions away from it. Freezing does not prove it was empty. 65 pointers elsewhere in the repo still read "logged in ACTIONS.md" or "tracked in ACTIONS.md", including live ones in virt-advisor-registry.md (the 28-dormant-trees programme, broadening the urgency trigger coverage), server/collaborate/data/repository.js and BusinessPerformanceReport.vue. Read it once, end to end, and move anything still genuinely open onto this list.
items.risk: If a real open task exists only in the frozen file, nobody triages it - which is the exact failure the freeze was meant to prevent, moved rather than removed. The file's own warning says three items were once found already built while still flagged open, so expect most of it to be stale; the point is to prove that rather than assume it.

askedBy.detail: Raised by the session that froze the file, 2026-08-24, as the named cost of freezing it.

items.note: Do this before trusting the live list as complete. Until it is done, the honest statement is that the live list holds everything anyone has looked at recently, not everything that is open.

items.name: The to-do page’s hand-written half describes six finished items and misses ten live ones
items.why: `to-do.md` is a generated ranked table wrapped in hand-written per-item detail. Only the table is regenerated by `npm run to-do`; the prose is edited by hand and has drifted. As of 2026-08-24 it carries detail blocks for six items that are no longer live (2.9, 4.16, 4.19, 4.28, 4.29 and, until today, 4.7) and none at all for ten that are (4.15, 4.25, 4.27, 4.31, 4.33, 4.36–4.40). Only three live items have both. 4.7’s block also disagreed with its own data on score — the prose said 2, the JSON said 5.
items.risk: A reader cannot tell which half to believe, and the page is the human-readable front door to the work list. This is the same mechanism recorded in 2.9’s own closure: the generated table said one thing, the prose said another, and on 2026-08-24 a session read the wrong one and advised Mike to pick an item on a false basis. Nothing tests the prose against the data, so the drift is silent and grows every session.

askedBy.detail: Found 2026-08-24 while closing 4.7 — regenerating the table left a stale hand-written block behind, which exposed the wider gap. Nobody outside asked.

items.touches: `design/features/to-do.md` (the hand-written sections outside the generated region), and a guard in `tests/unit/toDoItems.test.js` comparing detail blocks to the live refs.
items.note: The fix is two jobs and the second is the one that lasts: remove or label the six stale blocks, then add the guard so this cannot recur. A guard that simply requires every detail block to name a live ref would have caught all six. Decide deliberately whether every live item MUST have a block — the four DONE/PARKED blocks (3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 4.8) are kept on purpose and carry an explicit label, so the rule is "labelled or live", not "live only".

items.name: A test flips a global switch mid-run and fails about one run in four
items.why: `tests/unit/cases.routes.test.js` — "502s when the case read itself fails in production" — sets `process.env.NODE_ENV = 'production'` and then awaits an async call before restoring it. `NODE_ENV` is global to the worker, so anything reading it inside that window sees the wrong value. Observed failing once in four full runs on 2026-08-24; passes in isolation (57/57) and passed on the immediate re-run.
items.risk: An intermittently red suite is worse than a reliably red one: it trains everyone to re-run rather than read, which is exactly how a real failure gets waved through. The pre-commit hook requires zero failures, so this will occasionally block a commit for no reason and be cleared by retrying — the habit that hides the next genuine break.

askedBy.detail: Observed 2026-08-24 during the 4.7 verification runs. Not caused by that change — the first full run after the install was green. Nobody outside asked.

items.note: The comment above the test already explains why NODE_ENV must be pinned there, so the intent is right and the mechanism is wrong. Prefer injecting the value the code under test reads, or restoring in a `finally`, over mutating a global across an await. ⚠ Confirm the diagnosis before fixing — it failed once and the reading above is inferred from the code, not from a reproduction.
